label: GO-only; larger after repeated unrewarded S1 visits, ambiguous policy
terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S1 u") ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("state", -3) == 1) * (tv("reward", -3) == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 1) * np.exp(-((choice + 0.5)**2))
explanation: Sparse feature (nonzero on 1.3% of steps) that is active only at GO. Its magnitude grows when the agent kept reaching S1 and S1 kept failing to pay: the previous trial ended in S1 and the trial before also reached S1 unrewarded, most strongly when the last trial was unrewarded too (largest weight); a1 S1 u as the last trial and an unrewarded S1 visit three trials back add smaller amounts. It is near zero after the agent reached S2. The magnitude is also larger when the policy is ambiguous or leans slightly to a2 (choice logit near -0.5), i.e. the agent is about to switch away from a1/S1 (lose-switch). All terms use only observed history plus the model policy, no future variables. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.30 (history only, without the policy term: 0.28), slightly above the additive all ceiling 0.27. Large activations often come in runs over consecutive trials that these history terms only partly capture.
